主要内容: On April 7, 2017, the SEC Division of Corporation Finance issued an updated statement regarding the impact of the Court of Appeals decision on the Conflict Minerals Rule. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit reaffirmed its prior holding that Section 13(p)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 13p-1 violate the First Amendment to the extent they require regulated entities to report to the Commission and state on their website that any of their products have 'not been found to be 'DRC conflict free.' On April 3, 2017, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia entered final judgment in the case and remanded to the Commission. Although the district court set aside those portions of the rule that require companies to report to the Commission and state on their website that any of their products 'have not been found to be 'DRC conflict free,' the court and the Court of Appeals left open the question of whether this description is required by the statute or is a product of the Commission’s rulemaking. The Division of Corporation Finance has determined that it will not recommend enforcement action to the Commission if companies only file disclosure under the provisions of paragraphs (a) and (b) of Item 1.01 of Form SD.
